content.1_the_regression_pyramid_in_2026:
| Layer | What it catches | 2026 tool of choice | When in CI |
|---|---|---|---|
| Static | Type errors, lint, dead code | TypeScript `strict`, ESLint, `oxlint`, expo-doctor | Every PR (sub-30s) |
| Unit | Pure logic | Jest / Vitest + `@testing-library/react-native` | Every PR |
| Component / Interaction | Hook + render regressions | RNTL, Storybook test runner, `react-native-reanimated` mock | Every PR |
| E2E (deterministic) | Full user flows, navigation, deep linking, async data | **Maestro** YAML flows on iOS simulator + Android emulator | Every PR (parallel) |
| AI-driven exploration | Regressions a hand-written flow would never imagine | **Callstack `agent-device`** loop with an LLM agent | Nightly + on PR label |
| Visual / pixel diff | Theme, layout, RTL, dynamic-type breakage | Maestro `assertNoVisualDiff` / Percy / Chromatic for RN | Every PR |
| Real-device matrix | OS-version, OEM, biometric, locale, perf | **Maestro Cloud** or **BrowserStack App Automate** | Nightly + pre-release |
| Runtime / production | Crashes, ANRs, slow frames | Sentry, EAS Insights, Bugsnag | Always-on |
| Release | Store metadata, screenshots, version codes | EAS Submit + EAS Update | Tag / cron |

Maestro alone covers roughly rows 4–6; the other rows are non-negotiable because Maestro flows only catch what you scripted.

---
content.2_maestro_the_deterministic_e2e_core:
* **Repo / license:** `mobile-dev-inc/maestro` on GitHub, MIT, actively maintained (4 k★+ in 2026).
* **What it is in 2026:** A YAML-flow runtime for iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter, and web, with three SKUs:
  1. **Maestro CLI** (open source) – local runs on simulator/emulator or attached devices.
  2. **Maestro Studio** – desktop IDE that records flows visually and now ships an AI assist for generating flows from a prompt (Feb 2026 changelog).
  3. **Maestro Cloud** – managed parallel runner with video playback, flake analytics, and a `maestro record` MCP integration.
* **Why teams switched from Detox/Appium:**
  * Sub-1% flake rate claimed (vs. ~5–10% historically for Detox/Appium in surveys).
  * Zero app-instrumentation: just `npm i -g @mobile-dev-inc/maestro-cli` and you can drive any RN/Expo build.
  * Built-in tolerance primitives: `extendedWaitUntil`, `retry`, `assertNoVisualDiff`, `inputText` against React Native `TextInput`s that other tools routinely mis-handle.
  * Native handling of Hermes/JSI iOS sims, expo-dev-client screens, and New Architecture.
* **CI integration recipe (GitHub Actions, the most common path in 2026):**
  ```yaml
  # .github/workflows/maestro.yml
  name: maestro-e2e
  on: pull_request
  jobs:
    ios:
      runs-on: macos-14
      steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        - uses: expo/expo-github-action@v8
        - run: npx eas-cli build --platform ios --profile ci --non-interactive --no-wait
        - run: npx maestro test .maestro/ --include-tags=smoke
        - uses: mobile-dev-inc/action-maestro-cloud@v1   # optional: uploads artifacts + flakiness analytics
          if: always()
          with: { api-key: ${{ secrets.MAESTRO_CLOUD_KEY }} }
    android:
      runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
      steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        - run: npx eas-cli build --platform android --profile ci --non-interactive --no-wait
        - run: npx maestro test .maestro/ --include-tags=smoke
  ```
  Community `dniHze/maestro-test-action` is the lightweight alternative for shops that don't need Maestro Cloud analytics.

* **Sample flow (`.maestro/login.yaml`)** — note the `extendedWaitUntil` tolerance:
  ```yaml
  appId: com.example.app
  ---
  - launchApp
  - extendedWaitUntil:
      visible: "Sign in"
      timeout: 15000
  - tapOn: "Email"
  - inputText: "[email protected]"
  - tapOn: "Password"
  - inputText: "hunter2"
  - tapOn: "Sign in"
  - assertVisible: "Welcome back"
  - takeScreenshot: artifacts/login.png
  ```

* **Visual diffing in Maestro 1.40+:** `assertNoVisualDiff: { threshold: 0.02, baseline: baselines/login.png }` — baselines live in git, diff is uploaded to Maestro Cloud (paid) or stored as a GH Actions artifact.

---
content.3_callstack_agent_device_the_ai_explorat:
* **Repo:** `callstack/agent-device` (MIT). Created Jan 2026 by Callstack (React Native core contributors and Expo partners).
* **What it actually is:** A CLI that exposes device automation as discrete, agent-friendly commands. It is **not** an E2E framework and **not** a Maestro competitor — it is the "eyes and hands" for an LLM agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, etc.) to drive a device while a coding task is being verified. It also ships an **MCP server** so any MCP-capable agent (Cursor, Claude Desktop) can drive a real device as a tool.
* **Inspect-Act-Verify loop:** Every command returns a token-efficient accessibility snapshot with stable `@ref` IDs. The agent reasons over the snapshot, picks a command, runs it, and re-snapshots — the same loop Vercel popularized for web via `agent-browser`, ported to native iOS/Android/TV/desktop.
* **Capabilities in v1.x (mid-2026):**
  * Platforms: iOS sim, Android emu, physical devices, tvOS, Android TV, visionOS sim, macOS, Linux desktop browsers.
  * Backends: Apple `simctl`/`XCTest`, Android `adb`/`UiAutomator2` (`uiautomator2` and `xcuitest` are explicitly listed as engine topics).
  * Skills pack: bundled `skills/` directory with ready-made sub-agent prompts (smoke-test, perf profile, accessibility audit, RN dev-menu capture).
  * Evidence capture: every action auto-saves a `evidence/` folder of screenshots + AX trees for postmortems.
* **Where it fits in the regression stack:**
  1. **PR-time "fuzz loop":** a GitHub Action spins up an agent (Claude Sonnet 4.5 or GPT-5), gives it the diff, and tells it to find a regression using `agent-device` driving the EAS dev client. Result is a structured pass/fail + screenshot evidence attached to the PR.
  2. **Nightly exploratory suite:** the same loop, but with broader budgets, runs against real iOS/Android in BrowserStack.
  3. **Local developer loop:** devs run `npx agent-device doctor` and `agent-device open` from terminal; Claude Code can call it as an MCP tool to self-verify changes before commit.

* **Tiny example** (Claude Code driving the tool):
  ```
  $ agent-device open com.example.app --platform ios
  $ agent-device snapshot -i
  @e2 [button] "Allow notifications"
  $ agent-device press @e2 --settle
  $ agent-device screenshot ./evidence/01.png
  ```

* **What it doesn't replace:** It is too slow and too non-deterministic to gate every PR on. That's why the 2026 playbook is "Maestro for everything you know + `agent-device` for everything you don't."

---
content.4_device_farms_real_device_clouds:
* **Maestro Cloud** (`mobile.dev`) – official first-party runner, parallel sharding, video replays, historical flake dashboard, baseline visual diff storage. Best DX, premium pricing.
* **BrowserStack App Automate** – now first-class for Maestro. Documents `app-automate` integration; ships real iOS device farm and Android device farm. Strong for legacy / older-OS coverage.
* **Sauce Labs** – supports Maestro via Appium bridge for shops that already pay for Sauce.
* **AWS Device Farm / Firebase Test Lab** – still Maestro-compatible only via Detox/Appium paths in 2026, but Expo's `eas-cli` has shortcuts.
* **DeviceCloud.dev** – community/cheaper alternative marketed at "Maestro Cloud but ~50 % cheaper".

CI orchestration rule of thumb in 2026: run on **simulator/emulator in PR** (cheap, parallel, fast) and gate **release branches** with a smaller real-device matrix (1× latest iPhone + 1× low-end Android) inside the same workflow.

---
content.5_ci_orchestration_eas_workflows_is_the_:
If the app is an Expo app, **EAS Workflows** (`.eas/workflows/*.yml`) is now the canonical orchestrator. It runs the same EAS build infrastructure you already pay for and supports a first-party `test:maestro` job type as of mid-2025:

```yaml
# .eas/workflows/maestro-pr.yml
name: PR Maestro
on:
  pull_request: {}

jobs:
  build:
    type: build
    params: { platform: ios | android, profile: ci }
  test:
    type: test
    params:
      testType: maestro
      flow: .maestro/smoke
      requires:
        - build
```

EAS Insights, the bundled observability product, surfaces Maestro pass-rate and flakiness over time and is now what most Expo teams use instead of a third-party dashboard.

For non-Expo React Native or bare workflows, the standard pattern is:

1. **Build** the `.app`/`.apk` once via EAS Build (or `fastlane`/`xcodebuild` + `gradlew assembleRelease`).
2. **Install** into the simulator/emulator and run Maestro.
3. **Shard** the flow directory by tag or filename across N runners (GitHub Actions matrix, Buildkite, CircleCI).
4. **Archive** evidence (screenshots, recordings, accessibility trees) to S3/Artifactory.
5. **Gate** the merge via required-status-check.

---
content.6_end_to_end_pipeline_architecture_recom:
```
PR opened
  │
  ├── static / unit / RNTL  (GitHub Actions, <2 min)
  │
  ├── eas build --profile ci   (EAS Build, parallel iOS+Android, ~5 min)
  │      │
  │      └── eas test maestro   (EAS Workflows Maestro job, ~3-5 min)
  │              - sharded by tag: smoke, auth, checkout, a11y
  │              - assertNoVisualDiff against baselines in repo
  │
  └── (label: ai-explore)  GitHub Action
        └── spawns Claude Sonnet 4.5 + agent-device MCP server
            against the EAS dev-client build
            → posts PR comment with pass/fail + screenshots

Merge to main
  │
  ├── Nightly cron: agent-device on real-device matrix (BrowserStack)
  │
  └── On tag: eas build → eas submit → store screenshots for review
```

This stack means:
* The PR gate is fast, deterministic, and uses **Maestro** on simulators.
* **Callstack `agent-device`** runs as a label-triggered "exploratory fuzz" — catching the regressions no human would write a test for (gesture edge cases, accessibility misses, native-modal edge cases).
* **Real-device coverage** lives on a cron and on release branches — not on every PR.
* **Runtime telemetry** (Sentry + EAS Insights) catches whatever escapes all of the above and feeds back into new Maestro flows.

---
content.7_what_state_of_the_art_looks_like_in_pr:
1. **Flow-as-code in YAML checked into git.** Every product PR ships a matching `.maestro/*.yaml` flow. CI fails if flows are stale relative to the screens they cover.
2. **Tag-based sharding.** `smoke`, `auth`, `checkout`, `pay`, `a11y`, `regression-deep`. CI fans out across runners.
3. **Visual diff baseline PR.** When the first flow is merged, its screenshots are committed as baselines. Subsequent PRs get an automated "visual diff" report attached.
4. **AI fuzz labelled.** A `ai-explore` label triggers the `agent-device` MCP loop; results are non-blocking but visible.
5. **Deterministic + non-deterministic split.** Maestro = deterministic gate. `agent-device` = intelligence layer. They share the same `evidence/` directory so you have one source of truth.
6. **EAS Insights dashboard.** Flake rate, slow-flow detection, OS-coverage heatmap, and CI-vs-prod crash correlation — surfaced in PRs and Slack.
7. **Schema-mocked backend.** All Maestro flows run against a deterministic mock service (MSW / WireMock) so E2E never flakes because of a third-party API.
8. **Hermes + New Architecture parity.** Maestro is one of the few tools that drives Hermes-JSC and Bridgeless mode reliably in 2026, so the CI build uses the same JS engine as production.

---
content.8_decision_matrix_when_to_use_what:
| Situation | Best 2026 tool |
|---|---|
| Write E2E for a happy-path user journey | Maestro (CLI + Cloud) |
| Build a flow visually without code | Maestro Studio |
| Catch regressions no human thought to test | Callstack `agent-device` with Claude/GPT agent |
| CI for an Expo app in 2026 | EAS Workflows (`type: test`, `params.testType: maestro`) |
| Need real iPhone/iPad real-device coverage | BrowserStack App Automate (Maestro) or Maestro Cloud |
| Pixel-perfect regression on UI | Maestro `assertNoVisualDiff` + Percy/Robot Framework |
| Pure unit/component coverage | Jest + `@testing-library/react-native` |
| Hermes/bridgeless visual debugging | Maestro CLI with `--device` + `react-devtools` |
| Performance regressions (frames, jank) | Maestro + `agent-device perf-profile` skill, or `flipper-plugin-rnperf` |

---
content.9_sources_and_further_reading:
* **Maestro project** – `https://github.com/mobile-dev-inc/maestro` and docs at `docs.maestro.dev`.
* **Callstack `agent-device`** – `https://github.com/callstack/agent-device`, introduced January 2026; site `https://agent-device.dev/`.
* **EAS Workflows docs** – `https://docs.expo.dev/eas/workflows/syntax/` (last edited July 2026); includes a `test` job with `testType: maestro`.
* **BrowserStack Maestro integration** – `https://www.browserstack.com/docs/app-automate/maestro`.
* **Maestro Cloud** – `https://maestro.dev/cloud` (parallel runs, video replay, baseline visual diff).
* **Mission Lane case study** – "Building Confidence in Mobile Deployments with Maestro & Percy visual snapshots" (Nov 2025), a representative 2026 reference architecture.
* **Community GH Action** – `dniHze/maestro-test-action` (lightweight alternative to the official `mobile-dev-inc/action-maestro-cloud`).
* **Detox vs Maestro comparison** – Maestro's Feb 2026 industry report places Maestro as the 2026 default for RN/Expo shops that want low-flake, no-instrumentation flows.

---

### TL;DR

**August 2026 best practice for React Native / Expo regression prevention:**

> Use **Maestro** YAML flows as the deterministic E2E backbone, run them in parallel on every PR via **EAS Workflows** (or GitHub Actions + Maestro Cloud / BrowserStack), use **Callstack's `agent-device`** as an AI-driven exploration and verification layer (label-triggered or nightly), back them with a real-device nightly matrix for release branches, layer Jest/RNTL and visual-snapshot checks underneath, and close the loop with **EAS Insights** + Sentry in production. Maestro answers *"did this PR break the flows we wrote?"* and `agent-device` answers *"did this PR break anything we didn't write a flow for?"* — together they cover the regression surface that no single tool could cover alone.
</answer>
